出版者的话

古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：“任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。

现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。

情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期。一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心发展影响很长远。

当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。

这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。

让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧

Publisher's Note

The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry; that's not difficult. But to get angry at the right time, in the right place, with the right person, and in the right way—this is truly difficult.' What we now call emotional management is precisely about expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time, in the right place, and toward the right person.

In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills, because those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this skill, though perhaps intelligent, often struggle in their endeavors.

While emotional management skills may partly stem from innate factors, they ultimately rely on learning and cultivation over time. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this period create lasting neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.

Currently, the practice of parent-child co-reading emotional management picture books is widely recognized as an effective way to cultivate emotional intelligence. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried into children's ears by parents' voices, taking root in their hearts, and growing with sunlight and rain.

This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks addresses specific emotional topics for children, illustrating their inner journeys and revealing how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a valuable reference for parents during shared reading.

Let us enjoy a wonderful parent-child reading journey together with this series.

老师对你说
与人为善，与己为善
儿童文学作家保冬妮说过：“阅读是人生中一件无比奇妙和令人享受的事情，而图画书是带领孩子进入阅读的最有效的通道。”好的绘本总会带给我们美的享受、温暖的感觉。
《小鼹鼠的惊喜》中的小鼹鼠在家门口捡到了一个奇怪的包裹，她打开包裹，发现里面有一个不知道是什么的小宝宝。于是，小鼹鼠喂宝宝吃了奶，然后带着宝宝去找妈妈了。兔子、熊、狗獾……哪一个才是宝宝的妈妈呢？赶路时，大灰狼出现了，小鼹鼠会遇到危险吗？一波三折之后，小鼹鼠终于把宝宝送回了妈妈身边。故事结束了吗？当然没有。因为家里没有了宝宝，显得空荡荡的，正当小鼹鼠觉得难过时，一个大大的惊喜出现了——朋友们拿着礼物来到她家！原来，今天是小鼹鼠的生日，而她完全忘记了……可她的朋友们没有忘呀！
合上书，意犹未尽，仿佛看到小鼹鼠欢快、热闹的生日派对了。
在这温馨美好的亲子阅读过程中，家长们和孩子共同欣赏小鼹鼠的故事，相信孩子一定会深深喜欢上这只小鼹鼠。她的热心，她的善良，她的勇敢，她的执着，温暖了别人，也温暖了自己。“送人玫瑰，手有余香”，正是因为小鼹鼠总是热心帮助别人，才收获了好朋友的关心和爱护。

page_text_en:
Teacher Says to You
Be Kind to Others, Be Kind to Yourself
Children's literature writer Bao Dongni said: "Reading is an incredibly wonderful and enjoyable experience in life, and picture books are the most effective way to lead children into reading." Good picture books always bring us beautiful experiences and warm feelings.
In "The Mole's Surprise," the little mole finds a strange package at her doorstep. She opens it and discovers a baby whose identity is unknown. So, the little mole feeds the baby milk and then takes the baby to find its mother. Which one is the baby's mother—the rabbit, the bear, or the badger? On the way, the big bad wolf appears—will the little mole be in danger? After many twists and turns, the little mole finally returns the baby to its mother. Is the story over? Of course not. With the baby gone, the house feels empty. Just as the little mole feels sad, a big surprise appears—her friends come to her house with gifts! It turns out today is the little mole's birthday, and she had completely forgotten... but her friends hadn't!
Closing the book, one feels a lingering sense of joy, as if seeing the little mole's cheerful and lively birthday party.
In this warm and wonderful parent-child reading experience, parents and children together enjoy the story of the little mole. Children are sure to deeply love this little mole. Her kindness, her goodness, her bravery, her perseverance—she warms others and warms herself. "When you give a rose, your hand still smells of its fragrance." It is precisely because the little mole always helps others with kindness that she gains the care and affection of her good friends.

“嗯嗯……”猫头鹰思索着，“像这样的小动物，我记得动物园里有，就在森林的另一边……”
page_text_en:
The little mole slowly recovered from her shock and told the other animals how the package was found at her doorstep.
"Hmm..." the owl thought, "Animals like this, I remember, are in the zoo, over on the other side of the forest..."
summary_zh: 小鼹鼠向狗獾和猫头鹰讲述熊猫宝宝包裹的来历，猫头鹰回忆起类似动物可能在森林另一边的动物园里。
小鼹鼠抱着熊猫宝宝来到动物园的熊猫展区，背景中有熊猫和小熊猫在竹林中，展板上写着“熊猫”二字，画面右下角有二维码和宣传文字。

page_text_ocr_zh:
小鼹鼠来到动物园，悄无声息地走过各种围栏。
突然，她在一 个指示牌前停了下来：
“是他！就是这样的宝宝！”
“请问有人吗？”她小声地问道。
一只巨大的熊猫，迈着沉重的步子走了过来
page_text_en:
The little mole arrived at the zoo, quietly walking past various enclosures.
Suddenly, she stopped in front of a sign:
"It's him! That's exactly the kind of baby!"
"Is anyone here?" she whispered.
A huge panda walked over with heavy steps.
summary_zh: 小鼹鼠在动物园里寻找熊猫宝宝的同类，她在一个围栏前停下，认出了一只巨大的熊猫，并轻声呼唤它。

page_text_ocr_zh:
“我的宝宝！是我的宝宝回来了！”熊猫太太高兴地喊起来，激动万分！
“谢谢您啊，鹤女士！”
“呃……没什么！”小鼹鼠回答道，然后匆匆地离开了。
page_text_en:
"My baby! My baby is back!" Mrs. Panda shouted happily, overwhelmed with emotion!
"Thank you so much, Ms. Crane!"
"Uh... no problem!" replied the little mole, then hurried away.
summary_zh: 熊猫太太在动物园认出了自己的宝宝，激动地喊叫并感谢小鼹鼠，小鼹鼠则谦逊地回应后匆匆离开。

page_text_ocr_zh:
回到家，小鼹鼠觉得好难过。
家里没有了小“包裹”，显得空荡荡的。
可突然……
“咚-咚-咚！”
是谁在敲门呀？
page_text_en:
Back home, the little mole felt very sad.
Without little 'Package' at home, it felt empty.
But suddenly...
"Dong-dong-dong!"
Who is knocking at the door?
summary_zh: 小鼹鼠回到家后感到难过，因为熊猫宝宝不在了，家里显得空荡荡的，这时突然传来敲门声。
画面描绘了一场热闹的生日派对，小鼹鼠站在门口，戴着黄色帽子，双手合十，面带微笑，似乎在迎接客人。熊、獾、猫头鹰和小松鼠等动物朋友戴着生日帽，手持气球和鲜花，正开心地迎接她。背景有彩旗和彩纸屑，气氛温馨欢乐。

page_text_ocr_zh:
“生日快乐！
原来，今天是小鼹鼠的生日。
她完全忘记了……可她的朋友们没有忘呀！
